svg.title: Prime-zeta codebook
svg.desc: Left: a word's id picks a prime on a log ladder, the prime sets angles on eight clock dials, one per zeta zero, and the dials pick one of 256 cells on a 16 by 16 board, each cell holding 16 words. Right: the random start collapsed 4,096 words into 16 piles of 256 identical patterns; the prime-zeta table spreads them over 256 cells of 16 distinct words. Distinct vectors go from 16 to 4,096 and reachable development rows from 1,986 to 14,287.
svg.text: Prime-zeta codebook: every word gets its own fixed address
Construction: word → prime → eight angles → one cell
log scale; circled = one word’s prime
γk = imaginary part of zeta zero k; hands drawn for p = 11
angles pick a root per block
16 piles of 256 words with identical vectors.
Ties go to the lowest id.
Dial hands and cell positions are illustrative. The counters are a host check on the 14,287-row development panel, not a language result.
